cells.tense: You are here, with the pen, and the shared good thing is arriving as it comes.
cells.act: gather the scattered thoughts into one line
cells.ask: Write down the one thing the people in front of you are actually here for, then say that thing out loud and let the room keep it.
cells.core:
You can feel a good thing arriving with people — something worth marking, worth saying out loud together — and you're meeting it as it comes instead of bracing. You're thinking clearly enough to see what's actually here, and laughing at the real thing rather than the nearest joke. That's a room where people stay.

The next good thing doesn't need better props. Gather the scattered pieces of what this is about — the thing you're all actually here for — into one line, then say that line out loud and let the room take it from there. You get to hold complexity and a full room at once, and what enters lands where it can land.
cells.sheetLine: A good thing is entering, and you're here for it.
cells.place: arriving at the threshold, where what was outside comes in

cells.tense: You're bracing at a good thing that hasn't even arrived yet.
cells.act: commit to the long build and do today's part
cells.ask: Before you do another thing, return to the one you already started and stay with it for today's part, and don't add anything else.
cells.core:
The celebrating hasn't arrived yet, and you're already building for it — booking, planning, bracing for the next high while the people in front of you are still standing in this one. You're performing the fun instead of having it. The intensity that should be lightness has pinned you to the future, and even the good things have started to ask you to prepare for them.

The way back is a build already underway. Return to something you have already begun — the craft, the work, the thing that keeps asking for you — and stay with it for today's part before the next celebration comes. Commitment is not another preparation. It's the opposite: you make this one thing, here, and the future can't actually be built ahead of its time.
cells.sheetLine: You're celebrating something that hasn't happened yet.

cells.tense: A good thing was here, and you're still standing at the door it already came through.
cells.act: go all the way into the pattern until you meet its edge
cells.ask: Pick one thread of what you keep turning over and follow it past where it usually gets uncomfortable, to the edge, just once.
cells.core:
The good thing is already here — the people, the celebration, the thing worth marking — and you're still at the door it came through. Under-expressing means the joy is thin in the room and you're not quite in it, watching from just behind yourself. The threshold has already been crossed; you're the one still standing there.

Don't push yourself into the party. The way back is one level down. Pick one thread of what you have been thinking about this — a thought, a pattern, the thing you keep turning over — and follow it past where it usually gets uncomfortable, to the edge, just once. The depth you find there won't be about the occasion. It will be the ground you stand on when you step through.
cells.sheetLine: The door is behind you, and you're still standing at it.
cells.place: arriving at the threshold, where what was outside comes in

cells.tense: You're gathering people toward something and calling it nothing you're doing.
cells.act: bring the two sides of your thinking into one plan
cells.ask: Write out the two sides you keep carrying apart — the thing you want and the thing you're afraid of — and put them on one page as one plan.
cells.core:
A good thing is gathering people — something worth celebrating is coming into the room — and you're the one gathering them. Ask and you'd say it's just how the group is. The room arrives because you make the call, set the thing in motion, decide the moment is worth marking, and you don't name that as yours.

One small act of authorship brings it back: bring the two sides of your thinking into one plan. Write the thing you want and the thing you're afraid of on the same page, as one plan, and keep the page. You have been holding the pieces separately and calling it the group's shape. They are yours, and on one page they can actually hold.
